items.text: Duquesne is a pillar in Pennsylvania’s higher education system. I enjoyed a visit this morning with @Duqedu President Gormley, Dean Kauffman, and Joe Rockey. We toured the College of Medicine to see the innovative ways technology is being used to advance healthcare at this teaching hospital.

Pennsylvania is proud to host the new National Guard training center at Penn State Health Milton S. Hershey Medical Center – the only such center on the East Coast. An inaugural cohort of 3 Air National Guard members underwent trauma and EMS training at the new center earlier this month. They then participated in a capstone mass casualty simulation event to earn their graduation from the program. My team was honored to be there to congratulate the very first graduating class of this prestigious program!

Many people might be unaware that the mushroom capital of the world is Kennett Square, Pennsylvania, employing nearly 10,000 people and contributing nearly $1.3 billion to the local economy. @USDA’s crop insurance program should be available to all farmers, and I’m hopeful that this yearlong study yields much needed coverage to protect Pennsylvania’s mushroom farmers. I look forward to working on this and other agriculture initiatives with my PA colleagues in the House and the Senate.

Students in career and technical schools across the Commonwealth are studying to join the next generation of PA’s workforce, and Upper Bucks County Technical School (UBCTS) is one of the leaders in this space. UBCTS offers programs in manufacturing, healthcare, IT, law enforcement, and emergency services to over 900 students in the southeast region. My team toured UBCTS’s facility in Perkasie, PA, to learn more about the institution’s growth, industry partnerships, and their commitment to preparing students for in-demand careers.

The support provided by @TheArcPA to vulnerable individuals and their caregivers across the Commonwealth can be lifechanging. My team in the midstate attended the Arc’s 2nd annual Disability Health Action Summit in Hershey, PA, to learn more about the theme of the summit, which is to “Advance Health Equity for People with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities.” I’m grateful for the work that groups like the Arc do to advocate for Pennsylvanians with disabilities and their families.

Community health centers are the backbone of accessible, affordable care, and I’m committed to strengthening them, so that every family has the support they need to live healthy, full lives. Today, I had the privilege of touring the Maria de Los Santos Health Center in Philadelphia, which serves as a vital resource for the community. Thankful to all the health care workers in our Commonwealth—I see your work and I value it, and I’m fighting to make sure you have the resources and workforce support you need.

Had a great meeting with Erie Insurance leadership to discuss their redevelopment projects and to commemorate their 100th anniversary, which they celebrated just this past weekend. Erie Insurance is the largest employer in the county, and I look forward to collaborating with them to address key issues like housing affordability, workforce development, and insurance regulations.

Ryan Aument, our State Director, was proud to represent our office at the Harrisburg Regional Chamber’s Policy Pulse Speaker Series this month. He shared our key priorities and engaged with business, nonprofit, healthcare, education, and government leaders from across the Harrisburg region. I remain committed to supporting policies that strengthen PA’s business community and create opportunities for growth. Thank you to the Chamber for hosting this important conversation.

It’s time to put politics aside and stop these vicious, personal attacks against Senator Fetterman, his wife, and his health. While we have many differences, we are both committed to working together to achieve results for the people of Pennsylvania and make their lives better. He is authentic, decent, principled, and a fighter. These disgraceful smears against him are not the John that I know and respect.

Thousands joined my latest telephone town hall to hear real, unscripted Q&A on the issues that matter most—like the cost of health care. These conversations keep me informed on what my constituents care about most.

Hear my take on tackling health care costs: https://t.co/HcQ0roZfFt

It’s obvious that the radical left is viciously attacking Sen. Fetterman for not toeing their party line. Let’s put politics aside & stop these personal attacks on John, his wife, & his health. He’s a good colleague & I’ll continue to work with him to deliver for our constituents.

Some constituents have been asking about Medicaid cuts. Most Americans want to cut waste, fraud, & abuse within the program while preserving benefits for the vulnerable individuals it's intended to help. I spoke about this issue earlier this week with @DawnStensland. Listen ⬇️

To be clear: I don’t support removing Medicaid benefits from the vulnerable people they are intended to help. But, I do back the President’s push to restore fiscal sanity and cut down on the waste, fraud, and abuse that’s gotten out-of-control over the past four years. https://t.co/QkrVNJAC6B

I fully agree with @POTUS — we should not cut Medicaid benefits. At the same time, I've always supported rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse, but never at the expense of those in need of the benefits. Listen to how I explained my position on this important issue on my recent telephone townhall:

While we must stop the flow of fentanyl that is ravaging communities in Philadelphia and across the state, we must also tackle the addiction crisis and help recovering addicts find dignity and self sufficiency. Yesterday I joined @PhillyMayor at Riverview Wellness Village to see firsthand how bold leadership is changing lives and helping recovering addicts find their way. By integrating housing, recovery, health, and workforce training, the Mayor and her team are helping set a new national standard for combatting the opioid crisis. I look forward supporting this initiative however I can and watching it help those who need it most.

Great way to start the week with a workout and then a short visit to my alma mater, Bloomsburg High School. This morning, we’re headed to Berwick for an exciting announcement. Stay tuned! https://t.co/GbAFA8HViC

Our nurses and healthcare workers are incredibly important to our Commonwealth. Last week, my team and I met with advocates from the American Organization for Nursing Leadership on how we can encourage nursing education and support our robust medical industry in Pennsylvania. https://t.co/tx347cJWrl

Spent Saturday morning with members of the incredible team at @ChildrensPgh. The innovative and lifesaving work they’re doing on behalf of courageous young patients like Jade exemplifies so much of what makes Pennsylvania truly the land of “eds and meds.” https://t.co/gGjCj5DjHv

I’m so glad to see this bipartisan legislation introduced in the PA Senate. Removing phones from classrooms will not only help students focus, but also protect them from the harmful effects of social media that too often interfere with learning and mental health. https://t.co/NBlLhF5ldz

Relieved to learn that both troopers involved in the shooting in Susquehanna County earlier today - Trooper Joseph Perechinsky and Trooper William Jenkins - are in stable condition as they receive treatment for their injuries. Their courage and bravery surely kept community residents safe from danger today, and for that we are grateful for their service.

✅ Lowering Costs: By voting to renew the Trump tax cuts, increase and make permanent the Child Tax Credit to $2,200, raise the standard deduction that 90% of taxpayers claim, make the Paid Family and Medical Leave credit permanent, and create new deductions to fulfill the promise of no tax on tips and no tax on overtime – all signed into law by President Trump.

I support access to safe, effective vaccines like measles and Hep B. I also hear a lot of skepticism directed at the public health establishment, especially in the wake of COVID and the mistreatment of those who did not get the COVID shot. We need public health rooted in science and trust and we need to get this right.

Had a productive meeting with Pike County leaders yesterday – including my friend Bill Rosado, Warden Craig Lowe, and County Commissioners Matt Osterberg and Ronald R. Schmalzle.

We discussed my continued support for rural healthcare, the impacts of a government shutdown, and ensuring Pike County – the fastest-growing county in PA – has the resources it needs to thrive.

We are working together to keep Pike County a great place to live, work, and raise a family.

Great start to the week visiting with Anson Flake at Aurelius in Harrisburg. Aurelius is a brain health and human performance lab that is taking a holistic approach to treating PTSD, TBI, and the other challenges so many of our nation’s veterans face. I’m grateful to Anson and his team for their commitment to helping our military heroes overcome the mental wounds of war and make the successful transition back to civilian life.
Read my op-ed in the @PittsburghPG: https://t.co/o4SSlyCdSJ
